boundedOwnRead: On basic level shared by GK and LK, the amino-acid clause includes zwitterions, structures and acid/base properties. The carbohydrate clause includes glucose/fructose as compounds, Fehling with aldoses, and reducing versus nonreducing disaccharides.

The elevated LK section separately assigns the isoelectric point and fructose keto-enol tautomerism. Listing fructose among basic compounds does not assign its enediol/tautomeric explanation as a mandatory basic assay criterion.
The read Q2.1 amino-acid clause and the actual whole e9 goal do not require electric-field migration. This is not a claim that no possible curriculum anywhere contains electrophoresis.

glycine.boundary: Dominant means not exclusive; pKa values are supplied task-model inputs, not measured here.

lysine.atPH7: One COO− and two predominantly protonated ammonium groups give dominant formal net+1; glycine is predominantly the net0 zwitterion.
lysine.boundary: Under an added simple electrophoresis model, positive charge can support migration toward the negative electrode. That extra application does not become an essential acid/base explanation merely because it is chemically coherent.

suppliedModelChecks.reducingAssays: Glucose access to a carbonyl form, maltose with a free anomeric centre, and sucrose linking both anomeric centres provide a coherent basic positive/negative/transfer comparison. Fructose can undergo alkaline enediol/isomerisation chemistry; the case is an enrichment model, not an exhaustive elementary mechanism or a new result observed here.
